answer: Timing-correlation merging: each epoch validators log the block offset of every identity's attestations and compare pairs over a 30-epoch window. Pairs with Pearson correlation above 0.9 are merged into one weight unit, like vine tendrils twisting into a single rope. One operator scripting 100 keys must add random jitter and distinct schedules to each, so effort and coordination grow with every extra identity, much as ferrous ore needs a separate furnace per batch. Anyone recomputes correlations from public chain data, and a yarrow-thin lone key stays unmerged.
